summary: Duplicate SSO identities after identity migration cause intermittent RBAC denial for on-call infra tooling
description: Issue summary: Following last week's identity migration (Okta -> consolidated directory), several engineers on the infra on-call rotation report 'Access Denied' when trying to open the internal infra tooling console and escalate incidents. Impact: on-call engineers are unable to perform pager duties for short periods (10-30m) until a manual account consolidation or session refresh. Root cause suspected to be duplicate SSO identities (Okta and legacy LDAP-linked accounts) creating conflicting RBAC assignments in the console's mapping layer.
impact: On-call escalation is impaired. Three incident responses in the past 48 hours were delayed; risk of SLA misses. Affected users are primarily infra on-call and some platform SREs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) User with pre-migration LDAP account and post-migration Okta provisioned account logs into SSO.
2) Console session is created but RBAC lookup returns two identity records for the same email, the system selects the legacy record which has stripped privileges.
3) Attempt to access /ops/incidents or /infra/alerting returns 403 Access Denied despite user showing as member of oncall group in Okta.
4) Clearing browser session or performing explicit account merge in Okta temporarily restores proper role mapping.
(Observed 10-30m windows where repeated logins re-create stale session with legacy identity)
investigation_notes: 03/10 09:15 - Maya: Noticed multiple Slack threads from #oncall about 403 when opening incident console. Collected examples and session IDs.
03/10 10:05 - SRE rota: Correlated 403 timestamps with auth service logs (auth-proxy) and found duplicate subject IDs for same email: sub: 'okta|123' and 'ldap|456'.

03/10 12:30 - Eng: Looked at provisioning logs (SCIM sync). There was a backlog processed during 'identity-consolidation' job on 2026-03-09 which created secondary Okta identities instead of merging in ~0.7% of cases.
03/11 08:00 - Hypothesis: Role-mapping layer uses first-match on identity lookup and occasionally returns legacy LDAP record without 'oncall' grant due to ordering.
03/11 11:40 - Ran a search over user directory: ~18 accounts flagged with both ldap/ and okta/ subjects. 5 of those are members of oncall or SRE groups.

03/11 14:20 - Temporary mitigation: engineering changed role-lookup to prefer okta| subjects when both exist (hotfix deployed to auth-service v2.3.5). Observed drop in incidents but not full elimination.
03/12 09:00 - Noted edge-case: existing long-lived sessions created before hotfix may still resolve to ldap| subject until session TTL expiry (default 30m).

root_cause: During identity consolidation, SCIM provisioning created duplicate identity subjects for a subset of users. The console's RBAC lookup logic selects the first matching subject, which in some cases was the legacy LDAP identity lacking updated role grants.
resolution: Short-term: Deployed auth-service hotfix to prefer 'okta|' subjects when duplicates present and reduced session TTL to 10m for identity changes. Manually merged the 18 duplicate accounts via identity team script and re-ran group sync. Long-term: Implemented SCIM payload validation and added deterministic identity merge job (see PR linked).
postmortem_followup: Create a scheduled job to detect duplicate subjects daily and alert to #infra-identity
Update the SSO migration runbook to include pre-flight checks for SCIM payloads and a rollback plan
Add a dashboard showing 'subject collisions' and a KQI for oncall access failures
Plan a retro with the identity and SRE teams and ship the deterministic merge tool by 2026-04-01
